name: New Bough
desc: A sword made from sacred wood, said to have once turned the tide of battle.

customize.name: Beyond the Chrysalis
customize.desc: A longsword brimming with light and color, and as weightless as a butterfly when brandished. It was once used by a certain individual to break bonds.

customize.name: Hymn of the Maelstrom
customize.desc: An exquisite lamp crafted out of blue chalcedony which looks like a treasure right out of a fairy tale. It is said that a song of praise, forgotten by all, slumbers sealed inside this lamp.

customize.name: Breezeborne Refrain
customize.desc: A dark green bow string made out of pure and flawless gemstone. It never fails to summon a warm spring breeze whenever it is drawn.

customize.name: New Bough
customize.desc: A sword made from sacred wood, said to have once turned the tide of battle.

customize.name: Winter's Heavy Heart
customize.desc: A ceremonial artifact formed from the purest ice and snow. Legend has it that generations of Snegovik lords used it in coronation ceremonies until five hundred years ago.

customize.name: Dragon's Bane
customize.desc: A polearm decorated with an entwining golden dragon. Light and sharp, this weapon may very well kill dragons with ease.

customize.name: Favonius Greatsword
customize.desc: A heavy ceremonial sword of the Knights of Favonius. It channels elemental power easily and is highly destructive.

value.text:
When the equipping character hits the opponent with an attack within 12s after using the Elemental Skill, they gain the "Verdant" effect, which increases their ATK by <color=#36ffff>4%/5%/6%/7%/8%</color> and their Elemental Mastery by <color=#36ffff>20/25/30/35/40</color> . This effect lasts 6s and can trigger once every second. Max 3 stacks. The aforementioned effects can still trigger even when the equipping character is not on the field.
Radiance: Stellar Glimmer: The effect of "Verdant" is changed to: Increases ATK by <color=#36ffff>6%/7.5%/9%/10.5%/12%</color> as well as Stellar Glimmer reaction DMG dealt by the equipping character by <color=#36ffff>8%/10%/12%/14%/16%</color> .

materials.desc: Common currency. The one language everybody speaks.

materials.name: Measured Pour of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
The radiance that once gleamed like the aurora in the northernmost sky was extinguished when it met the gaze from high above.
The calamity of bitter cold and black crystal nearly destroyed the foundations upon which all life endured.
Only the fae, unafraid of the cold, were able to emerge from the ice and snow to rule over the deserted realm.

materials.name: Hollow Root of Life
materials.desc:
A branch dropped by a Leshy before it returned to silence.
With only a few crystals grown upon it, this branch holds little power and gives off a faint glow.

materials.name: Chimeric Core
materials.desc:
The internal core harvested from aberrant man-made monsters.
This is the most fundamental core grown within a man-made monster. Yet, simple as it may be, it contains the primordial design for the growth of all man-made creations.

materials.name: Mora
materials.desc: Common currency. The one language everybody speaks.

materials.name: Intoxication of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
What others enjoy as a festive indulgence after a bountiful grain harvest is a necessity of survival for the clans who walk through the bitter cold.
It is said that the Domovoy, whose mastery of brewing was without equal, once relied on this art to enrich the treasury of the king they served.
And so, passed from clan to clan through trade, the fae's brew flowed across the frozen lands like honey laced with poison.

materials.desc:
A branch dropped by a Leshy before it returned to silence.
A branch bearing a fair number of crystals. It feels heavy in the hand, and traces of vitality can still be felt within it even after it has broken away from the Leshy's body.

materials.name: Symbiotic Chimeric Nucleus
materials.desc:
The internal core harvested from aberrant man-made monsters.
A relatively complex core harvested from a man-made monster. This symbiotic nucleus is engineered to sustain the biological cycles of two distinct life-forms, seamlessly weaving them into a single organism.

materials.name: Exhilaration of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
Legend has it that long ago, countless casks of fine wine were poured into a frozen lake.
Some say the wine was intended as wartime provisions, which had to be destroyed after some mishap. Others say a certain Grand Duke of the Domovoy had lost a bet to the ruler of the Water Imps.
Only when unquenchable azure hellflame spread across the lake, and the foes below writhed in choking waves, did they come to understand:
In the hands of the people well versed in the turning of the world, water itself could burn, and even the sweetest nectar could prove deadlier than poison.

materials.desc:
A branch dropped by a Leshy before it returned to silence.
A branch with a fully formed crystal core. It contains vitality that will not easily fade. If buried in the soil, it would likely grow into a new Leshy before long.

materials.name: Prime Chimeric Nexus
materials.desc:
The internal core harvested from aberrant man-made monsters.
The most complex core a man-made monster can possibly sustain, serving as an artificially engineered yet flawless seed of life. Whoever brought this creation into life has surely unlocked the very secrets of how life itself is shaped.

materials.name: Revelry of the Cellared Spiritual Nectar
materials.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
The Grand Duke of the Domovoy commanded the crystal mines and the development of the frozen lands. To him, carving an oasis out of the polar wastes was a mere trifle, and importing rye of better quality was no difficult task either.
Even among the many fae nobles who had endured in Snezhnaya to this day, none could rival the splendor of his status.
Yet the flame of ambition burned ever brighter, licking its way down his throat, while the ancient fae's greed swelled with the years and knew no end.

desc.text:
Of all the stories handed down from the ancient forest, only the bird with wings drawn close is willing to sing them before the world.
Its song begins amid the splendor of spring, in an age when peace had endured for centuries and the forest had grown deep beneath a wealth of branch and leaf.
Yet as the season turned, the ice began to thaw and run in streams along the riverbed, carrying with it from lands still bound in frost the distant ringing of arms.
Soon, none could halt the advance of the Blood-Devourer, and across the snowy realms, every nation was brought before the same cruel choice: to bow or to perish.
The treeborn, however, whose roots reached back beyond even the frozen earth, still remembered their gracious lords of old, for that memory endured in the ordering of their leaves and in the rings that traced their wood.
Though the golden bough had long lain broken, though lofty dreams had fallen to ruin, and nations once resplendent as the morning stars had vanished beneath boundless fields of ice,
The descendants of the forests still desired no part in strife, wishing only to remain faithful to the peace they had kept since ages immemorial.
Even the Knyazhna of Blood, for all her tyranny, had never sought to exterminate their kind — much less, they believed, would the Volkodlak who bore the name of wisdom.
Until the bird returned, at the season when it should have settled upon tender new boughs, only to behold the haze of battle rising in every quarter.
For no greater offense than declining, with all due courtesy, the summons to pledge themselves to the Volkodlak, the holy forest left behind by the dawn-star had been consumed in flame.
Thus, when the King of the Pale Star came at last with his chosen retinue, scarcely a tenth of the ancient treeborn remained alive.
Unbidden tears slipped from the eyes of Vaselisa, daughter of the King of the Water Imps, as she mourned in song the countless lives so unjustly taken.
While Strivozha, saint of the Vila, wept until no words would come, and beseeched the King of the Pale Star to grant the forest his protection as well.
"O King Lesnik, venerable grandsire of the wilderness and of the myriad forests, I am Monomakh, heir to the Pale Star and bearer of the Pale Crown."
"I have come to end the strife of this world and bring peace upon the earth. I would found a realm of mercy and forgiveness, where no living creature shall ever come to harm again."
"O King Lesnik, venerable grandsire of the wilderness and of the myriad forests, I therefore come before you with a plea, though I do not ask that your kin spill their blood in my name."
"I ask only for such healing herbs and leaves as you might bestow upon us, that my companions may tend the wounds borne by the earth."
The great lord of the trees looked down upon the young golden-haired boy, as a Vila might look upon the Domovoy dwelling far below.
The canopy murmured, and after a silence steeped in ages of ancient pride, all that long-held reserve yielded at last to a single weary sigh.
Then a venerable bough broke from the ancient tree, and the bird took it gently into its beak, bore it forth, and laid it before the golden-haired youth.
"Go forth, young king. See your promise fulfilled, and make of this world a peace everlasting, beyond all sorrow and unrest."
"Into your keeping I give my life, and no barrier wrought of shadow shall turn aside its edge."
"Mourn not the dead, for all who draw breath must in time sink back into the dust. This truth I learned long ago."
"Yet though they return to dust, the forest shall remember. When spring comes again, the new-grown branches and leaves shall carry that memory onward."
